Sheppard, an AmLaw 50 firm, is seeking an associate (4-8 years) to join our Finance Practice Group in Dallas. Sheppard, Mullin, Richter & Hampton LLP is a global Am Law 50 full-service law firm with over 1,200 attorneys across 16 offices worldwide, advising clients on high-stakes litigation, complex transactions, and cutting-edge regulatory matters across key industries—including energy, real estate and development, financial services, healthcare, and technology. Our teams deliver practical, business-oriented counsel and collaborate seamlessly across offices to support clients locally, nationally, and internationally. Sheppard is known for its collaborative and transparent culture. The Finance Practice Group advises financial institutions, private credit funds, and private equity sponsors on a wide range of complex finance transactions. This role offers direct client contact and substantial opportunities for business development, along with exceptional training and career development and a clear path. The ideal candidate will have experience in the following areas: Executing finance transactions, including acquisition financings Drafting and negotiating credit agreements and related closing documentation Lender side and/or borrower side leveraged finance experience is a plus Qualifications: Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school 4-8 years of experience working on varied finance transactions Resume, cover letter, and law school transcript are required to apply. Candidates must be admitted to and a member in good standing of the Texas bar. The annual salary range for this position is $310,000 - $435,000. Candidates with eight (8) or more years of relevant experience may be considered at the Special Counsel level, commensurate with qualifications and experience. Contact: For inquiries, please reach out to Katherine Milanes at kmilanes@sheppard.com . Req #: 2026-25987

lateral.Position: Los Angeles – Corporate (M&A) – Mid-to-Senior Level – Associate
lateral.Job Description: Skadden’s M&A team in the Corporate practice of the Los Angeles office is seeking an outstanding lateral candidate (class of 2022-2020) with broad experience working on a variety of public and private M&A transactions and the ability to work effectively as part of a deal team across practices areas. High level of academic achievement and peer firm experience preferred. Qualified candidates should be admitted to practice law in California. The starting base salary for this position is expected to be between $310,000 to $390,000 annually. Actual salary will be determined based on skills, experience (to the extent relevant) and other job-related factors, consistent with applicable law. This position may be eligible for a discretionary year-end bonus. Associates who join Skadden laterally participate in an enhanced mentor program, which specifically focuses on the unique needs experienced attorneys face during professional transitions. These efforts, along with our professional development and other Skadden benefits , including a hybrid work model*, offer a dynamic environment where all can shape their own career trajectories while contributing to groundbreaking legal work. We also have an extensive pro bono program that allows attorneys to devote, and receive credit for, time for myriad causes that spark their interests and matches those interests with the legal needs in the community. *Our current hybrid work model consists of working Monday through Thursday in the office. Attorneys also receive the opportunity to work remotely for specified periods throughout the year. EEO Statement Skadden is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Applicants who require an accommodation during the application process should contact Alex Taylor at (212) 735-2176. Skadden will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance. lateral.Offices: Chicago, Illinois; New York, New York; Washington, D.C.
lateral.Job Description: Crowell & Moring is an international law firm with operations in the United States, Europe, and MENA. Drawing on significant government, business, industry, and legal experience, the firm helps clients capitalize on opportunities and provides creative solutions to complex regulatory and policy, litigation, transactional, and intellectual property issues. The firm is consistently recognized for its commitment to pro bono service, as well as its comprehensive programs and initiatives to advance the professional and personal development of all members of the Crowell community. Job Description Crowell & Moring LLP, a global Am Law 100 law firm, seeks a highly qualified professional track/staff trademark associate to join its Advertising & Brand Protection ​practice group, in Washington, D.C., New York, or Chicago. This is a full-time, professional (non-promotion) track attorney position. Qualifications A minimum of 5 years of extensive domestic and international trademark prosecution experience, 10+ years of experience preferred Extensive experience in trademark portfolio management, Extensive experience reviewing trademark search reports and preparing written trademark clearance opinions Experience monitoring trademark watch notices and preparing written recommendations when warranted Experience with trademark enforcement, including prepare cease-and-desist letters, and handling oppositions and cancellation actions before the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board, Experience managing international trademark matters and communicating with foreign trademark practitioners Experience with trademark licensing, and due diligence projects Have excellent academic and professional credentials as well as highly developed writing, analytical, and communication skills Candidates must be a member of the state bar for the office to which they are applying or otherwise eligible for admission by waiver. All candidates should have excellent academic credentials as well as highly developed organizational, writing and analytical skills. How to Apply To apply, submit your resume, transcript, and writing sample using the online application system. Benefits and Compensation Crowell & Moring LLP offers a competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits package. Our benefits include healthcare, vision, dental, retirement, and all-purpose leave and progressive options such as back up childcare, wellness programs, cultural events and social activities. We take great pride in our positive, friendly culture that rewards hard work and success, at the same time recognizing the importance of family and community service. Our Firm is committed to fair and equitable compensation practice in accordance to applicable laws. The salary range for this position is $190,000 to $240,000. Additional compensation may include a discretionary bonus. Other benefits include healthcare, vision, dental, retirement, and all-purpose leave. The salary for this position may vary based on market data, an applicant’s skills and prior experience, certain degrees and certifications, and other factors. SEARCH FIRMS: submissions from search firms will NOT be accepted by email . To submit your candidate, apply through our applicant portal. lateral.Job Description: The New York office of Blank Rome LLP has an opening for a Trusts & Estates Attorney with at least 6 years of experience. Candidates must have in-depth, broad-based experience in estate planning and estate administration, and exempt-organizations experience is preferred. An LLM in Tax is strongly preferred, as well. Candidates must be self-motivated, personable team players, have outstanding academic and professional credentials and be admitted to practice in New York. Florida admission is a plus. Successful candidates will have an opportunity for significant professional growth and client contact. This position is open to recruiting agency submissions at this time . The target annual pay range for this role in New York is $310,000 - $450,000. Positions outside of New York will be subject to annual pay ranges specific to the market for that particular geographic location. Actual pay will vary depending upon various factors, including relevant experience and skillset. The compensation range listed is just one component of Blank Rome’s total compensation package for employees. Other monetary rewards include bonuses based on performance. In addition, Blank Rome provides a comprehensive suite of benefits to promote health and financial security, including medical, dental, and vision insurance as well as life, accident, and disability insurance plans. The firm also provides the opportunity to participate in 401(k) retirement benefits, commuter benefits, and well-being programs. All headhunter submissions must be directed to Erica Rovinsky ( Erica.Rovinsky@blankrome.com ). Do NOT submit via web application.

Ballard Spahr LLP is seeking a mid-level privacy litigation associate to join its Privacy and Data Security Litigation Practice in Minneapolis. This is a litigation role focused on defending privacy-related claims, including individual and class action matters brought under statutes such as the California Invasion of Privacy Act (CIPA), the Federal Wiretap Act/Electronic Communications Privacy Act (ECPA), the California Comprehensive Computer Data Access and Fraud Act (CDAFA), the Video Privacy Protection Act, other state wiretap and eavesdropping laws, and common law invasion of privacy. The ideal candidate will have 3-5 years of relevant litigation experience, either through a law firm or clerkship. Excellent writing skills, attention to detail, and strong academic credentials are required. Our Privacy and Data Security group represents a wide range of local, national and international clients in individual and class action claims related to privacy and cybersecurity matters. Ideally, the firm seeks a candidate with experience litigating privacy and class action matters. Candidates should have a strong desire to responsibly and thoughtfully integrate artificial intelligence tools into their legal practice. This is an excellent opportunity for professional growth in a collegial team environment of a national law firm. Active bar license in Minnesota, or the ability to waive in, is required. How to Apply: Ballard Spahr is a nationally recognized law firm with more than 750 lawyers across 19 offices in the United States. A career at Ballard Spahr means joining a team of talented mentors, colleagues, and friends, supported by strong leadership that actively encourages professional growth. To apply, please submit a resume, law school transcript, writing sample and cover letter (optional) through our online application system. Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Compensation and Benefits: The salary range for this position is from $210,000 to $245,000, which reflects the Firm’s good faith and reasonable estimate of possible compensation at the time of posting. Actual pay will depend on several factors such as the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Effective January 1, 2027, the annual salary range for this position will be $230,000 to $270,000. In addition to the salary for this position, lawyers may be eligible for an incentive bonus program and/or a profit-sharing bonus program. lateral.Job Description: Position Overview The eDiscovery Review Attorney supports the firm's litigation teams by conducting first-level and second-level review of documents in connection with litigation, regulatory investigations, and internal investigations. This is an entry-level position designed for attorneys seeking to build foundational skills in eDiscovery, with opportunities to take on additional eDiscovery responsibilities over time. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, possesses strong analytical skills, and is eager to grow within a collaborative, technology-driven legal environment. Key Responsibilities The eDiscovery Review Attorney reviews documents for relevance, privilege, confidentiality, and responsiveness designations in hosted review platforms such as Relativity and Everlaw. The role requires applying legal judgment to identify privileged communications, work product, and confidential materials, and to escalate complex privilege or substantive issues to supervising attorneys. The attorney codes documents according to established review protocols and applies issue tags as directed by case teams. The position involves performing quality control checks on reviewed documents, identifying and flagging potential hot documents for senior attorney review, and drafting privilege logs under the direction of supervising attorneys. Over time, the eDiscovery Review Attorney will support broader eDiscovery tasks, including assisting with search term development and validation, coordinating with eDiscovery team members on workflow setup, and contributing to the preparation and verification of document productions. Additionally, the role participates in team meetings, manages the review team, and assists with training new reviewers on project-specific protocols. The eDiscovery Review Attorney may also assist with organizing and summarizing reviewed materials for use by case teams in depositions, motions, or trial preparation. Required Qualifications The candidate must possess a Juris Doctor (JD) degree from an accredited law school and be a licensed attorney, active and in good standing, in any U.S. jurisdiction. The candidate must have at least one year of document review experience in a law firm, legal services company, or corporate legal department setting. Familiarity with Relativity or a comparable document review platform is required. The candidate must demonstrate strong attention to detail, the ability to maintain consistent coding accuracy across large document sets, and effective written and verbal communication skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience with technology-assisted review (TAR) or predictive coding workflows is preferred. Familiarity with the full electronic discovery lifecycle, including preservation, collection, processing, and production, is a plus. Compensation The annual base salary for this position ranges from $75,000 to $95,000, commensurate with experience and geographic location. The posted salary range reflects the entry-level nature of this role and the requirement for a licensed attorney with at least one year of document review experience.

Why Work Here Health, Wellness & Work-Life Balance We believe exceptional work begins with supporting the people behind it. That's why Greenberg Glusker invests in programs and benefits designed to promote the health, well-being, and work-life balance of our team members: Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and their eligible dependents, as well as life insurance, short- and long-term disability coverage, and accidental death and dismemberment insurance. Employees can also start a Health Savings Account (HSA) or Flexible Spending Account (FSA) to help save for healthcare costs. All full-time team members receive free, unlimited access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program, offering 24/7 counseling services, financial resources, legal consultations, and other wellness support. Beyond traditional benefits, we encourage healthy living through access to an on-site fitness center as well as our through our wellness webinars and challenges. We also provide paid time off and generous paid parental leave. Just as importantly, we foster a culture where attorneys are expected to respect one another's time, recognizing that personal well-being is essential to long-term professional success. Professional Development & Mentorship At Greenberg Glusker, we believe exceptional attorneys are developed through meaningful experience, thoughtful mentorship, and opportunities to build successful, long-term careers. This looks like: Early Responsibility & Meaningful Experience – Greenberg Glusker offers the best of both worlds: the sophistication of a leading law firm with the opportunities for early exposure that come with being a mid-sized practice. Our size allows associates to work directly with clients earlier, take on sophisticated legal work, and develop meaningful responsibility that serve as the foundation for a thriving career. A Dual-Mentor Program – Every new associate is paired with both a senior associate and a partner mentor. Senior associates – or “Big Sibs” – serve as day-to-day resources, providing practical guidance as associates navigate life at the Firm. In addition, each associate is matched with a partner-level mentor who offers broader career guidance, helping to chart a path for professional growth and long-term success. Hands-On Professional Development – We are committed to the continuous education and advancement of our attorneys. Through our Associate Training Program, attorneys engage in learning opportunities designed to strengthen legal, business, and practice-specific skills while receiving ongoing mentorship from experienced practitioners. A Voice in the Firm – Associates at Greenberg Glusker are encouraged to play an active role in the Firm's direction. Many serve on Firm committees where their ideas and perspectives are genuinely valued. Business Development Support – Building a successful legal career extends beyond practicing law. Associates have access to the Firm's marketing, public relations, and business development resources and are encouraged to attend events and conferences to develop relationships that fuel future practice growth. Diversity & Inclusion Founded in 1959 by lawyers who were not welcome in traditional law firms due to religious discrimination, our firm has always valued skill, dedication, and integrity above all else. That legacy continues to shape our commitment to excellence and inclusion in the legal profession, guiding how we recruit, retain, and advance talent at every level. We are intentional about fostering a supportive culture and inclusive workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging and has an equal opportunity to succeed. That same commitment extends beyond our walls, as we engage with the broader community through pro bono work, public interest partnerships, and initiatives aimed at promoting social justice and expanding access to the legal profession. Recent initiatives include: Pro bono partnerships benefiting low-income, underserved communities, with unlimited billable credit for associates Volunteer efforts and fundraising for a variety of causes that matter to the communities where we live and work Book scholarships for first-year law students in Southern California Longstanding participation in the Association of Corporate Counsel SoCal Summer Internship Program Leadership roles held by our attorneys in various legal and business organizations Support for mission-driven organizations and local businesses Internal and external programming, including educational events and community-building activities Giving Back Community involvement is an important part of Greenberg Glusker's culture. We believe giving back strengthens not only the communities we serve, but also the connections within our own Firm. In addition to our commitment to pro bono service, our team regularly participates in volunteer initiatives and charitable fundraising throughout the year. Recent examples include: Law Rocks Fundraiser – Greenberg Glusker’s in-house band, The Gee Gees, have participated three years in a row in the annual Law Rocks Los Angeles competition. The band has won the Judge’s Choice Award and has raised tens of thousands of dollars for local charities like Alliance for Children’s Rights and TreePeople. Starve-A-Vampire Blood Drive – In partnership with the American Red Cross, team members participate in our annual October blood drive, complete with festive decorations, refreshments, and music. Last year alone, 30 participants helped support up to 90 lives. Food From The Bar – Through creative fundraising events – including Pie-a-Partner, lip sync competitions, karaoke, casino nights, comedy shows, and magic shows – we have raised thousands of dollars for the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank. Adopt-A-Family – Every holiday season, our team comes together to provide gifts and support for families in need. Volunteer Service – From building homes with Habitat for Humanity to preparing meals at Our Big Kitchen Los Angeles, our team enjoys opportunities to serve the community together. A Culture of Appreciation At Greenberg Glusker, we profoundly subscribe to the belief that our workforce is our most valuable asset, and we pair that belief with action to ensure that our team members feel valued: Administrative Professionals Day – Each year, we recognize Administrative Professionals Day with a week of appreciation events, which have included firm-sponsored massages, catered treats, gifts, and attorneys serving breakfast to our staff. Personal & Professional Milestones – Throughout the year, we celebrate birthdays, work anniversaries, engagements, weddings, growing families, retirements, and other personal milestones through our firm newsletter and office celebrations. Years of Service Recognition – At our annual holiday party, team members receive a Greenberg Glusker lapel pin upon reaching five years with the Firm, and for every five years thereafter, a diamond is added to the pin – a meaningful tradition to honor long-term dedication and commitment. Building Community Beyond the Office Greenberg Glusker creates opportunities throughout the year for colleagues to connect outside of client work. Beyond the design of our Century City office, which features open kitchens and collaborative gathering spaces that encourage conversation, teamwork, and spontaneous connection throughout the day, examples include: Attorney Retreats & Ski Trips – Each year, our attorneys enjoy a weekend retreat in Ojai, California, as well as an annual ski trip, providing opportunities to build relationships, recharge, and connect outside the office. July 4th Family Breakfast – An annual summertime tradition where team members and their families gather for breakfast, face painting, balloon artists, crafts, and other family-friendly activities. Private Movie Screenings – Whether celebrating the release of a highly anticipated film or one our attorneys helped bring to life, we host private screenings at the AMC Century City theater, often inviting team members to bring a guest. Halloween Celebration & Office Trick-or-Treating – One of our most anticipated annual traditions, Halloween at Greenberg Glusker features festive decorations, themed lunches, costume contests, and office-wide trick-or-treating for employees' children, with candy stations hosted across all three floors. Thanksgiving Potluck – Before the holiday, team members gather to share homemade dishes while the Firm provides turkey and other favorites. Those who prefer not to cook can instead support the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank through a charitable donation, making the event a celebration of both community and giving. And Much More – Throughout the year, you'll also find escape rooms, happy hours, Office Olympics, cocktail-making classes, office mini golf, and other opportunities to relax, celebrate, and enjoy time together.

Qualifications: Greenberg Glusker is seeking a junior corporate associate (2–3 years of experience) to join its nationally recognized Corporate Group. The ideal candidate will have experience supporting M&A transactions, including conducting due diligence, drafting and reviewing ancillary documents, and assisting with transactions from due diligence through closing. Please note that only candidates who are currently admitted to the California Bar will be considered. Salary range: $210,000 – $230,000 per year For specific inquiries, please contact recruiting@greenbergglusker.com . Why Work Here: Health, Wellness & Work-Life Balance We believe exceptional work begins with supporting the people behind it. That's why Greenberg Glusker invests in programs and benefits designed to promote the health, well-being, and work-life balance of our team members: Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and their eligible dependents, as well as life insurance, short- and long-term disability coverage, and accidental death and dismemberment insurance. Employees can also start a Health Savings Account (HSA) or Flexible Spending Account (FSA) to help save for healthcare costs. All full-time team members receive free, unlimited access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program, offering 24/7 counseling services, financial resources, legal consultations, and other wellness support. Beyond traditional benefits, we encourage healthy living through access to an on-site fitness center as well as our through our wellness webinars and challenges. We also provide paid time off and generous paid parental leave. Just as importantly, we foster a culture where attorneys are expected to respect one another's time, recognizing that personal well-being is essential to long-term professional success. Professional Development & Mentorship At Greenberg Glusker, we believe exceptional attorneys are developed through meaningful experience, thoughtful mentorship, and opportunities to build successful, long-term careers. This looks like: Early Responsibility & Meaningful Experience – Greenberg Glusker offers the best of both worlds: the sophistication of a leading law firm with the opportunities for early exposure that come with being a mid-sized practice. Our size allows associates to work directly with clients earlier, take on sophisticated legal work, and develop meaningful responsibility that serve as the foundation for a thriving career. A Dual-Mentor Program – Every new associate is paired with both a senior associate and a partner mentor. Senior associates – or “Big Sibs” – serve as day-to-day resources, providing practical guidance as associates navigate life at the Firm. In addition, each associate is matched with a partner-level mentor who offers broader career guidance, helping to chart a path for professional growth and long-term success. Hands-On Professional Development – We are committed to the continuous education and advancement of our attorneys. Through our Associate Training Program, attorneys engage in learning opportunities designed to strengthen legal, business, and practice-specific skills while receiving ongoing mentorship from experienced practitioners. A Voice in the Firm – Associates at Greenberg Glusker are encouraged to play an active role in the Firm's direction. Many serve on Firm committees where their ideas and perspectives are genuinely valued. Business Development Support – Building a successful legal career extends beyond practicing law. Associates have access to the Firm's marketing, public relations, and business development resources and are encouraged to attend events and conferences to develop relationships that fuel future practice growth. Diversity & Inclusion Founded in 1959 by lawyers who were not welcome in traditional law firms due to religious discrimination, our firm has always valued skill, dedication, and integrity above all else. That legacy continues to shape our commitment to excellence and inclusion in the legal profession, guiding how we recruit, retain, and advance talent at every level. We are intentional about fostering a supportive culture and inclusive workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging and has an equal opportunity to succeed. That same commitment extends beyond our walls, as we engage with the broader community through pro bono work, public interest partnerships, and initiatives aimed at promoting social justice and expanding access to the legal profession. Recent initiatives include: Pro bono partnerships benefiting low-income, underserved communities, with unlimited billable credit for associates Volunteer efforts and fundraising for a variety of causes that matter to the communities where we live and work Book scholarships for first-year law students in Southern California Longstanding participation in the Association of Corporate Counsel SoCal Summer Internship Program Leadership roles held by our attorneys in various legal and business organizations Support for mission-driven organizations and local businesses Internal and external programming, including educational events and community-building activities Giving Back Community involvement is an important part of Greenberg Glusker's culture. We believe giving back strengthens not only the communities we serve, but also the connections within our own Firm. In addition to our commitment to pro bono service, our team regularly participates in volunteer initiatives and charitable fundraising throughout the year. Recent examples include: Law Rocks Fundraiser – Greenberg Glusker’s in-house band, The Gee Gees, have participated three years in a row in the annual Law Rocks Los Angeles competition. The band has won the Judge’s Choice Award and has raised tens of thousands of dollars for local charities like Alliance for Children’s Rights and TreePeople. Starve-A-Vampire Blood Drive – In partnership with the American Red Cross, team members participate in our annual October blood drive, complete with festive decorations, refreshments, and music. Last year alone, 30 participants helped support up to 90 lives. Food From The Bar – Through creative fundraising events – including Pie-a-Partner, lip sync competitions, karaoke, casino nights, comedy shows, and magic shows – we have raised thousands of dollars for the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank. Adopt-A-Family – Every holiday season, our team comes together to provide gifts and support for families in need. Volunteer Service – From building homes with Habitat for Humanity to preparing meals at Our Big Kitchen Los Angeles, our team enjoys opportunities to serve the community together. A Culture of Appreciation At Greenberg Glusker, we profoundly subscribe to the belief that our workforce is our most valuable asset, and we pair that belief with action to ensure that our team members feel valued: Administrative Professionals Day – Each year, we recognize Administrative Professionals Day with a week of appreciation events, which have included firm-sponsored massages, catered treats, gifts, and attorneys serving breakfast to our staff. Personal & Professional Milestones – Throughout the year, we celebrate birthdays, work anniversaries, engagements, weddings, growing families, retirements, and other personal milestones through our firm newsletter and office celebrations. Years of Service Recognition – At our annual holiday party, team members receive a Greenberg Glusker lapel pin upon reaching five years with the Firm, and for every five years thereafter, a diamond is added to the pin – a meaningful tradition to honor long-term dedication and commitment. Building Community Beyond the Office Greenberg Glusker creates opportunities throughout the year for colleagues to connect outside of client work. Beyond the design of our Century City office, which features open kitchens and collaborative gathering spaces that encourage conversation, teamwork, and spontaneous connection throughout the day, examples include: Attorney Retreats & Ski Trips – Each year, our attorneys enjoy a weekend retreat in Ojai, California, as well as an annual ski trip, providing opportunities to build relationships, recharge, and connect outside the office. July 4th Family Breakfast – An annual summertime tradition where team members and their families gather for breakfast, face painting, balloon artists, crafts, and other family-friendly activities. Private Movie Screenings – Whether celebrating the release of a highly anticipated film or one our attorneys helped bring to life, we host private screenings at the AMC Century City theater, often inviting team members to bring a guest. Halloween Celebration & Office Trick-or-Treating – One of our most anticipated annual traditions, Halloween at Greenberg Glusker features festive decorations, themed lunches, costume contests, and office-wide trick-or-treating for employees' children, with candy stations hosted across all three floors. Thanksgiving Potluck – Before the holiday, team members gather to share homemade dishes while the Firm provides turkey and other favorites. Those who prefer not to cook can instead support the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank through a charitable donation, making the event a celebration of both community and giving. And Much More – Throughout the year, you'll also find escape rooms, happy hours, Office Olympics, cocktail-making classes, office mini golf, and other opportunities to relax, celebrate, and enjoy time together.

Why Work Here Health, Wellness & Work-Life Balance We believe exceptional work begins with supporting the people behind it. That's why Greenberg Glusker invests in programs and benefits designed to promote the health, well-being, and work-life balance of our team members: Our comprehensive benefits package includes medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and their eligible dependents, as well as life insurance, short- and long-term disability coverage, and accidental death and dismemberment insurance. Beyond traditional benefits, we encourage healthy living through access to an on-site fitness center as well as our through our wellness webinars and challenges. We also provide paid time off and generous paid parental leave. Professional Development & Mentorship At Greenberg Glusker, we believe exceptional attorneys are developed through meaningful experience, thoughtful mentorship, and opportunities to build successful, long-term careers. This looks like: Early Responsibility & Meaningful Experience – Greenberg Glusker offers the best of both worlds: the sophistication of a leading law firm with the opportunities for early exposure that come with being a mid-sized practice. Our size allows associates to work directly with clients earlier, take on sophisticated legal work, and develop meaningful responsibility that serve as the foundation for a thriving career. Senior associates – or “Big Sibs” – serve as day-to-day resources, providing practical guidance as associates navigate life at the Firm. In addition, each associate is matched with a partner-level mentor who offers broader career guidance, helping to chart a path for professional growth and long-term success. Hands-On Professional Development – We are committed to the continuous education and advancement of our attorneys. Through our Associate Training Program, attorneys engage in learning opportunities designed to strengthen legal, business, and practice-specific skills while receiving ongoing mentorship from experienced practitioners. A Voice in the Firm – Associates at Greenberg Glusker are encouraged to play an active role in the Firm's direction. Many serve on Firm committees where their ideas and perspectives are genuinely valued. Business Development Support – Building a successful legal career extends beyond practicing law. Associates have access to the Firm's marketing, public relations, and business development resources and are encouraged to attend events and conferences to develop relationships that fuel future practice growth. Diversity & Inclusion Founded in 1959 by lawyers who were not welcome in traditional law firms due to religious discrimination, our firm has always valued skill, dedication, and integrity above all else. That legacy continues to shape our commitment to excellence and inclusion in the legal profession, guiding how we recruit, retain, and advance talent at every level. We are intentional about fostering a supportive culture and inclusive workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging and has an equal opportunity to succeed. That same commitment extends beyond our walls, as we engage with the broader community through pro bono work, public interest partnerships, and initiatives aimed at promoting social justice and expanding access to the legal profession. Recent initiatives include: Pro bono partnerships benefiting low-income, underserved communities, with unlimited billable credit for associates Volunteer efforts and fundraising for a variety of causes that matter to the communities where we live and work Book scholarships for first-year law students in Southern California Longstanding participation in the Association of Corporate Counsel SoCal Summer Internship Program Leadership roles held by our attorneys in various legal and business organizations Support for mission-driven organizations and local businesses Internal and external programming, including educational events and community-building activities Giving Back Community involvement is an important part of Greenberg Glusker's culture. We believe giving back strengthens not only the communities we serve, but also the connections within our own Firm. In addition to our commitment to pro bono service, our team regularly participates in volunteer initiatives and charitable fundraising throughout the year. Recent examples include: Law Rocks Fundraiser – Greenberg Glusker’s in-house band, The Gee Gees, have participated three years in a row in the annual Law Rocks Los Angeles competition. The band has won the Judge’s Choice Award and has raised tens of thousands of dollars for local charities like Alliance for Children’s Rights and TreePeople. Starve-A-Vampire Blood Drive – In partnership with the American Red Cross, team members participate in our annual October blood drive, complete with festive decorations, refreshments, and music. Last year alone, 30 participants helped support up to 90 lives. Food From The Bar – Through creative fundraising events – including Pie-a-Partner, lip sync competitions, karaoke, casino nights, comedy shows, and magic shows – we have raised thousands of dollars for the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank. Adopt-A-Family – Every holiday season, our team comes together to provide gifts and support for families in need. Volunteer Service – From building homes with Habitat for Humanity to preparing meals at Our Big Kitchen Los Angeles, our team enjoys opportunities to serve the community together. A Culture of Appreciation At Greenberg Glusker, we profoundly subscribe to the belief that our workforce is our most valuable asset, and we pair that belief with action to ensure that our team members feel valued: Administrative Professionals Day – Each year, we recognize Administrative Professionals Day with a week of appreciation events, which have included firm-sponsored massages, catered treats, gifts, and attorneys serving breakfast to our staff. Personal & Professional Milestones – Throughout the year, we celebrate birthdays, work anniversaries, engagements, weddings, growing families, retirements, and other personal milestones through our firm newsletter and office celebrations. Years of Service Recognition – At our annual holiday party, team members receive a Greenberg Glusker lapel pin upon reaching five years with the Firm, and for every five years thereafter, a diamond is added to the pin – a meaningful tradition to honor long-term dedication and commitment. Building Community Beyond the Office Greenberg Glusker creates opportunities throughout the year for colleagues to connect outside of client work. Beyond the design of our Century City office, which features open kitchens and collaborative gathering spaces that encourage conversation, teamwork, and spontaneous connection throughout the day, examples include: Attorney Retreats & Ski Trips – Each year, our attorneys enjoy a weekend retreat in Ojai, California, as well as an annual ski trip, providing opportunities to build relationships, recharge, and connect outside the office. July 4th Family Breakfast – An annual summertime tradition where team members and their families gather for breakfast, face painting, balloon artists, crafts, and other family-friendly activities. Private Movie Screenings – Whether celebrating the release of a highly anticipated film or one our attorneys helped bring to life, we host private screenings at the AMC Century City theater, often inviting team members to bring a guest. Halloween Celebration & Office Trick-or-Treating – One of our most anticipated annual traditions, Halloween at Greenberg Glusker features festive decorations, themed lunches, costume contests, and office-wide trick-or-treating for employees' children, with candy stations hosted across all three floors. Thanksgiving Potluck – Before the holiday, team members gather to share homemade dishes while the Firm provides turkey and other favorites. Those who prefer not to cook can instead support the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank through a charitable donation, making the event a celebration of both community and giving. And Much More – Throughout the year, you'll also find escape rooms, happy hours, Office Olympics, cocktail-making classes, office mini golf, and other opportunities to relax, celebrate, and enjoy time together.

**Description:** SFDA's Summer 2L Law Clerk Program is designed to recruit the most qualified 2L law clerks and train them for highly skilled legal work within the office. This program is only offered in the summer, and only 2Ls are eligible to apply.

**Why you should apply**

Our office is committed to supporting you in your growth through worthwhile, enriching, and educational experiences working for what we believe to be the best public law firm in the country.

**Details about working for the Attorney General’s Office**
The Office is committed to the benefits of a healthy life-work balance with a respectful, inclusive, and diverse workplace where you will experience belonging and be part of a supportive and collegial team. Successful candidates will join an office in which every person is committed to providing exceptional legal services and where individual professional development is encouraged and supported. Our work is also guided by our Anti-racist commitment to recognize, address and eradicate all forms of racism within the scope of our work and operations. Additional exceptional benefits of joining the AGO as a law clerk include:

- Competitive Salary: Law clerks who have completed their second year of law school will receive $24/hour.
- Law clerk positions assigned to our Seattle office locations receive an additional 5% King County Location Pay.
- Vacation Leave, Sick Leave, Military and Civil Leave, and Paid Holidays
- Health and wellness program.
- Access to attend a training and career development program that is recognized for its excellence and efficacy by AGOs nationwide.
- Enrollment in the Public Employees’ Retirement System, receiving one service credit for each month worked of 90 hours or more.
- _Due to the limited duration of these positions (less than six months), law clerks are not eligible for medical and dental benefits._

**Although each law clerk's experience is unique, the following duties are typical of an AGO law clerk: **

piSummerOpen.Organization: Americans United for Separation of Church and State
piSummerOpen.Job Title:
Summer Constitutional Litigation Internship
(Legal Department; remote)
piSummerOpen.Compensation: A stipend of $7,360 for a ten-week term
piSummerOpen.Job Description:
Americans United for Separation of Church and State is seeking full-time summer legal interns who are committed to civil rights, impact litigation, and upholding core First Amendment protections. 

**About Americans United. **Americans United is a nonpartisan educational and advocacy organization dedicated to advancing the constitutional principle of church-state separation as the only way to ensure freedom of religion, including the right to believe or not believe, for all of us. Founded in 1947, Americans United is a diverse and dynamic organization composed of people from all walks of life: lawyers and lobbyists, students and activists, religious leaders and impassioned Americans. Americans United includes people of faith and people who don’t profess any particular faith. 

For nearly 80 years, we have litigated church-state issues in federal and state courts across the country, with a substantial practice before the federal courts of appeals and the U.S. Supreme Court. Most of our cases involve novel, cutting-edge First Amendment and other constitutional issues. In recent years, for example, we have litigated lawsuits and submitted amicus briefs challenging or opposing:

·      Coercive religious practices in the public schools. 
·      Proselytizing by Trump-Vance Administration officials.
·      Public funding of religious education. 
·      Religion-based refusals by businesses, foster-care agencies, and government officials to provide services to LGBTQ+ people and religious minorities. 
·      Religion-based efforts to deprive people of access to abortion and contraceptives. 
·      Race-based and sex-based employment discrimination by religious employers.
For more information about Americans United’s legal program, please visit our website at [www.au.org](http://www.au.org/).

**Duties and responsibilities.** Legal interns receive substantive legal experience with in-depth exposure to some of the most important issues facing the nation. Interns assist with ongoing litigation by conducting legal and factual research and writing, analyze potential new litigation, and draft demand letters to resolve constitutional violations without filing suit. Interns may also draft pleadings, briefs, or discovery.
Our attorneys endeavor to prepare interns for public-interest legal practice, including by providing training and practical experience, in house and in conjunction with partner organizations. Interns are encouraged to take full advantage of the many events that take place in Washington, D.C., or are available virtually.

**Eligibility and requirements.** Law students (any year) who are committed to advancing the public interest and the separation of religion and government are encouraged to apply. Americans United includes and welcomes people of all genders, races, ethnicities, religions and beliefs, sexual orientations, gender identities, ages, socioeconomic backgrounds, and abilities. Because we work on a wide variety of issues and with many different communities, we value what diversity and diverse perspectives bring to our work.
 
_Research shows candidates from marginalized groups are less likely to apply for positions when they don’t meet 100% of the listed requirements; please consider applying even if you don’t match 100% of these criteria._
 
**Equal opportunity employer. **Americans United is an equal opportunity employer. We consider applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, marital or veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected status. If you need an accommodation for a disability to apply to this position, please let us know by emailing [hr@au.org](mailto:hr@au.org). 
 
**Compensation:** A stipend of $7,360 for a ten-week term. 
 
**Work Location:** Interns can work remotely from anywhere in the United States. There may also be opportunities to work in person in our Washington, D.C. office.
 
**Working conditions and physical requirements. **This position primarily involves working from a home office and/or professional office environment. The position requires routinely using standard office equipment such as computers, phones, and video-conferencing tools. It also requires the ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods, communicate effectively, and occasionally move about within the workspace. 
 
**How to apply.** **Please submit a cover letter, resume, law-school transcript, writing sample, and a list of three references through our web-based application portal at [bit.ly/AuscsBambooHR](https://bit.ly/AuscsBambooHR).** The cover letter should highlight why you want to work with us and what perspectives you would bring to strengthen our practice. The writing sample may be of any length; it should be your best example of comprehensive and detailed legal argument or analysis, should be your own work, and should not be substantially edited by anyone else. First-year law students who apply before receipt of their initial grades may submit a law-school transcript that shows their initial courses and an undergraduate transcript. If you have any questions about an internship position, please do not hesitate to contact us at [legaljobs@au.org](mailto:legaljobs@au.org).
 
**Deadline:** Positions will remain open until filled. Applicants are encouraged to apply by October 15, 2026.

piSummerOpen.Job Title: Opportunities for Law Students - Spring 2027 and Summer 2027
piSummerOpen.Job Description:
The Public Interest Law Project (PILP) is currently seeking applications from law students interested in joining our summer law clerk and extern programs for the **Spring 2027 term and Summer 2027**.

**The Public Interest Law Project (“PILP”)**
Since 1996, PILP has provided crucial litigation and advocacy support to local legal services and public interest law programs throughout California. Responding to the elimination of federal funding for state and national legal services support centers, PILP was established to ensure that local legal services programs could continue to participate in major litigation and advocacy on behalf of low-income people.

Today, PILP is one of California’s premier legal services support centers and works to advance racial and economic justice for low-income communities and communities of color by building the capacity of legal services organizations through impact litigation, trainings, publications, coalition building, and systemic advocacy. Our current priorities include work to: increase and preserve affordable housing; fight displacement; eliminate discriminatory zoning; support unhoused communities; prevent homelessness; and expand access to public benefits, income support, and supportive services. 

**What you will gain as a law clerk with PILP**
PILP law clerks receive mentoring and training from our highly skilled staff attorneys and gain exposure to the mechanics of litigation and state and local systems change advocacy while developing a better understanding of the legal barriers facing low-income and other underrepresented communities in California. PILP engages our law clerks in many phases of complex litigation. For example, we have involved clerks in all aspects of preparing an affordable housing/fair housing case for trial, including drafting discovery motions, participating in strategy sessions with co-counsel, and settlement negotiations with opposing counsel. Other law clerks have researched the legislative history and case law related to various provisions of affordable housing and public benefits laws; drafted portions of trial court and appellate briefs; assisted taking depositions; and drafted procedural and substantive legal memoranda, motions, and stipulations. Law clerks have also gone into the field, interviewing witnesses and drafting declarations for submission to the court.

Law clerks will also be considered for future fellowship opportunities for those who qualify.

**Funding**
Qualifying summer law clerks are eligible to directly receive an educational reimbursement of up to $5,250, with the possibility of additional stipend funding subject to PILP’s receipt of supplementary grant funds. (Full time summer law clerks will be required to show proof of payment on tuition or other educational expenses within the last 12 months to receive the educational reimbursement.)

Law clerk externs joining the program during the Fall or Spring terms will be eligible to receive school credit as available but will not receive direct funding.

**Deadlines**
The deadline to apply for the summer 2027 program is Friday, March 5, 2027. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
For all other law clerks planning to volunteer outside of summer, applications can be submitted on a rolling basis throughout the year. 

We offer either a fully remote schedule, or a hybrid schedule with up to 2 (two) in-person days working from our downtown Oakland office.

**How to apply for a clerkship with PILP**
Candidates should email application materials as word or pdf attachments to lawclerks@pilpca.org. If you prefer an alternative method of submitting these materials please contact us at the above email address. Please provide a cover letter that includes a brief statement of interest, résumé, writing sample (no more than 10 pages), and at least two professional references. In your cover letter, please also indicate your law school year and any past or current public interest law experience.

_The Public Interest Law Project (PILP) is an Equal Opportunity Employer and values a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. We strongly encourage people of color, women, people with disabilities, older adults, LGBTQ people, and individuals from other underrepresented groups to apply. It is PILP’s policy to prohibit discrimination and harassment of any type and to establish and maintain equal employment opportunities to all employees, volunteers, and applicants on the basis of union membership or activity, race, religious creed, religious observance, ethnicity, color, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or predisposition, military service, military and veteran status, pregnancy, child birth and related medical conditions, marital and family status, national origin, ancestry, age, medical conditions as defined by state or federal law, or disability, or any other basis prohibited by law._

piSummerOpen.Job Description:
New Hampshire Public Defender provides representation to clients facing criminal and delinquency prosecution in New Hampshire. We are a private, nonprofit corporation dedicated to ensuring that New Hampshire fulfills the constitutional mandate of equal justice for all citizens by providing high-quality representation for indigent defendants. The program’s attorneys, investigators, paralegals, social services and support staff span ten offices located across the state. We also provide appellate representation to clients through the Appellate Defender program. Our mission is to provide the best representation we can, and we strive to maintain a work environment that encourages attorneys to work creatively and zealously on behalf of clients. 

NHPD offers legal internships for students who want to become public defenders and who will have completed their 2L year by June 2027. The internship is a ten-week, full-time program. 2L interns obtain certification to appear in New Hampshire’s circuit and superior courts. Interns are assigned to one of NHPD’s ten offices and given an experienced attorney mentor who will supervise and guide them through their internship. The internship begins with two full days of group training taught by NHPD staff attorneys from across the state. Over the course of their internship, students typically interview clients, write and litigate motions, and represent clients at arraignment, bail, and probable cause hearings. They often represent clients in bench trials, and some have co-counseled jury trials and participated in jury selection, conducted examinations of witnesses, or delivered arguments to the jury.

The application process is competitive. NHPD seeks applicants who are strong students, have good potential as trial lawyers, have an interest in long term employment with NHPD, and show deep commitment to the representation of indigent criminal defendants.
Though the internship is unpaid, most interns are able to secure outside grants or school funding. Job-related expenses are reimbursed by NHPD. Interns must have a valid, unexpired drivers' license and access to an insured vehicle. 

This program is scheduled to begin on June 2, 2027, and conclude August 13, 2027.  Some flexibility on dates can be accommodated on a case-by-case basis. NHPD places interns in all of our trial offices and in our Appellate Defender office in Concord.

piExternOpen.Job Description:
The Clark County District Attorney’s Office in Las Vegas, Nevada is seeking motivated third year law students and law graduates for full-time Law Clerk positions within our Criminal Appellate Unit, Child Welfare Unit (Juvenile Division), and Civil Division. This is an excellent entry-level opportunity—most prosecutors in our office begin their careers as Law Clerks.
**Position Overview:**
 As a Law Clerk, you will engage in vital legal work that supports prosecution and public service, including:
- **Criminal Appellate Unit:** Drafting responses to appellate briefs, oppositions to post-conviction writs of habeas corpus, and other post-conviction motions.
- **Child Welfare Unit:** Conducting research related to child abuse and neglect cases in Family Court, assisting with policy and procedural advisories for the Department of Family Services, and addressing adoption, foster care licensing, and federal compliance issues.
- **Civil Division:** Conducting legal research and drafting memoranda on County Counsel matters.
**Key Details:**
- Bar membership is _not_ required during the one-year term of employment.
- Upon passing the Nevada Bar, Law Clerks are deputized and gain courtroom responsibilities.
- Law Clerks who pass the bar may apply for Deputy District Attorney positions during their term.
- JD completion by start date is required; current law students graduating before the start date are encouraged to apply.
- Start date is typically in the fall, allowing time to graduate, take the bar exam, and begin shortly thereafter—similar to judicial clerkship timelines.
**Why Join Us?**
 Working with the Clark County District Attorney’s Office means:
- Serving the community with purpose and impact
- Receiving dedicated mentorship and professional training
- Accessing clear opportunities for career growth and development
- Enjoying an exceptional work-life balance, including options for remote work
- Earning a competitive salary with merit-based raises and cost-of-living adjustments
- Qualifying for Public Service Loan Forgiveness
- Gaining unparalleled courtroom experience
- Being represented by a union that protects attorney rights
**Clark County’s Benefits Package Includes:**
- Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance
- Life insurance coverage
- 100% employer-paid retirement benefits
- Generous paid leave, including parental leave options
- Flexible work arrangements, including remote work opportunities where feasible

- Desire to be where our clients need them the most – on the border or in rural areas.
- Spanish-language fluency is a plus but not required. 
## **Here's how we can support you: **
- **Innovative Collaboration:** We're not just another legal program – we're your partners in creating fresh, effective solutions for our clients.  
- **Tailored Support:** We know each fellowship is unique. Whether it's EJW, Skadden, or other regional programs, we'll help tailor projects to fit your passion and our clients' needs. 
- **Limitless Possibilities:** The scope is yours to define. Dive into our diverse practice areas and pinpoint where you can have the most significant impact.

- **Housing Rights:** Fighting for fair housing practices and battling housing discrimination to ensure everyone has a safe place to call home. 
- **Employment Justice:** Standing up for workers' rights and combating workplace injustices. 
- **Juvenile Justice, Education & Special Education:** Protecting and empowering our youth through specialized legal services and support. 
- **Disaster Recovery:** Assisting communities in rebuilding and recovering after natural disasters.
- **Environmental Justice:** Representing low-income communities in protecting their resources. 

**TRLA IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER.**     
### **Interested in working with TRLA for your post-graduate fellowship? **

### **Submit your application by August 1.**

** **Open City Advocates seeks to host a Legal Fellow for projects through the Equal Justice Works Fellowship, Justice Catalyst Fellowship, and other public interest fellowships to begin in Fall 2027. Open City Advocates will consider any projects related to our mission, and we welcome the opportunity to discuss and develop project ideas with the applicant. 
 
**Organizational Background:**
Open City Advocates provides holistic legal representation to youth who have been committed to the DC Department of Youth Rehabilitation Services (DYRS) after sentencing in the juvenile justice system. This approach combines lawyering, advocacy, and mentoring to better guide youth through the system and set them up for success. Open City Advocates’ client-centered approach is foundational to the various systemic reform issues that we tackle with the juvenile justice system and the broader juvenile social service ecosystem.
	 
We tackle racial inequity in our juvenile justice system where it is most extreme, as 100% of youth who are committed to DYRS are youth of color. Based on the knowledge we gain from our direct client services, we then spearhead systemic reform efforts to end the revolving door of the juvenile and criminal justice systems, safeguard and expand due process protections, and encourage individualized, trauma-responsive services for court-involved youth.
	 
In 2020, the DC Court of Appeals ruled in our favor in our longstanding impact litigation case, _In re N.H.M. _(224 A.3d 581 (2020)). As a result of this decision, youth in DC’s juvenile justice system now have a clearly established right to an attorney throughout their commitment to DYRS. Open City Advocates is working with community partners to implement the right for all youth in DC. 
 
**Key Functions & Responsibilities (in addition to fellowship project): **
·      Individual Representation for DC Youth
o  Provide holistic, trauma-informed representation for approximately 5 youth committed to DYRS.
o  Attend team meetings and engage in informal client advocacy with DYRS.
o  Represent youth in institutional disciplinary hearings.
o  Represent youth in Community Status Review Hearings (revocation hearings).
o  Work with trial attorneys to provide mitigation information.
·      Support for Adult Clients
o  Support young people transitioning back to DC after a period of incarceration.
o  Draft sentencing letters in support of clients facing charges in DC Superior Court.
o  Connect clients to reentry and social services in DC.
o  Liaise with criminal defense attorney.
·      Systemic Advocacy
o  Attend coalition meetings with community partners.
o  Engage in systemic advocacy to support policies that support our youth and their families and communities.
** **

# **Why Start Your Legal Career in Texas?**
## **Because This is Where It Matters.**
It’s tough out here. The legal landscape is shifting, the attacks on our communities are relentless, and **access to justice is more critical than ever**. 
If you’re looking for comfort and predictability, this isn’t the place. But if you’re looking for a **fight worth fighting**—**one that changes lives**—**welcome to TRLA**. 
### **Defend the vulnerable, serve the community, sue the bastards. **
### **we litigate. hard.**
Federal court, state court, government agencies—you name it, we take cases there. Need expert witnesses? Depositions? We have a budget for that. If you’re not pushing your case forward, we will ask you why and offer support where needed. 
### **you won’t be alone.**
TRLA is one of the **largest legal aid programs in the country**, with nearly **200 attorneys**. You’ll be surrounded by experienced advocates who have spent their careers fighting for the people. They’re ready to work with anyone willing to push the limits with them. 
### **this work changes you.**
We’ve been doing this for over half a century, through political upheaval, funding crises, and legal assaults on our clients’ rights. No matter what, we keep showing up. The work you do with TRLA will shape you forever—leaving an indelible mark on your life, just as you leave yours on the fight for justice. 
### **the work you came to do.**
We serve the people who need us most—families on the Texas-Mexico border, refugees, low-wage workers, survivors of violence, and communities facing systemic injustice. We stop evictions, fight deportations, take on corrupt landlords and abusive employers, and push the law as far as it will go for our clients. 
### **don’t speak Spanish? not necessarily a dealbreaker.**
Many of our clients do, and while fluency helps, a little effort goes a long way. Show up, show respect, and we’ll help with the rest. 
### **name your practice area.**
We cover **over 40 areas of civil poverty law**—and if there’s one we’re missing, we’ll add it. Whether you want to do impact litigation, individual representation, or both, there’s room to shape your career here. 

### **the border is 1,200 miles long - pick your spot.**
We have **10 offices** along the Rio Grande. Find one that calls to you. Bring a classmate—we’ll office you together. 
**Coming back home?**
We love to see it. Nothing beats serving the community that raised you. 
**New to Texas?**
Welcome to the Lone Star State! Come for the work, stay for the people (and the tacos). 
### **what we offer (besides the work of a lifetime!):**
Starting salary: $66,929.20 for newly licensed attorneys 
- 100% IDR loan repayment assistance 
- Bar exam fee + bar prep paid 
- Healthcare, dental, and retirement plans 
- Pay + benefits start July 1—you start your work at the office the bar 
- Texas is a UBE state (min. score: 270), meaning your license is portable 
### **want to see it yourself?**
If we think you’re a fit, we’ll fly (or drive) you to the border for a tour of our offices. 
No obligation. Just come see the work in action. 
**This isn’t just a job. It’s a fight. If you’re ready, so are we.**

Description of Work
**Hourly pay rate will fall within stated range based on experience.**

The Assistant Public Defender (APD) is a trial lawyer position that supports the appointed Public Defender Director, playing a crucial role in countering state prosecutions. The APD practices in various forums, including county, municipal, and township courts, offering client-centered holistic legal representation to clients unable to afford legal counsel for criminal or civil violations. Additionally, the APD may be assigned to youth/juveniles under 18 years of age charged with criminal offenses and parents at risk of losing their children to the State because of allegations of neglect or abuse (N/A), and also sometimes serving as a Guardian ad Litem (GAL) in these cases. The position also provides operational/administrative assistance to the Director for recruiting, training, supervising, and evaluating a large volunteer and paid workforce of qualified student interns. While initially under supervision, the lawyer progressively gains independence with experience. As an APD progresses in the department, in addition to the tasks described above, the APD may be assigned to take on administrative duties, train and/or supervise subordinates, take leadership positions, and take on more difficult and/or higher jeopardy cases. 
Required Minimum Entrance Qualifications
1\. Must possess a Law Degree from an accredited college or university.
2\. Have a valid Michigan driver's license. 
3\. Must be eligible for Membership in the State Bar Association and be licensed to practice law in the State of Michigan. 
4\. Must be able to secure clearance to enter correctional facilities. 
5\. Must be able to provide personal transportation for job related duties throughout the County if a County-owned vehicle is not available.

**Preferred but not Required**
Bilingual in Spanish highly desired.
Two years of experience in the practice of criminal or family (i.e.: Neglect and Abuse, Juvenile, Probate (Mental Health) law is preferred.
Physical Conditions / Work Location
**PHYSICAL ACTIVITIES**
An Assistant Public Defender performs generally sedentary work activities, requiring the occasional lifting of objects weighing thirty-five (35) pounds or less.

**ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS**
An Assistant Public Defender works in a variety (i.e. County Courthouse, Jail, Public Defenders Office, etc.) of locations and additional travel may be required.
**This position may be in the Criminal Division or the Family Division.**

The selected candidate must take a post-offer medical examination (including back screen and complete physical) and drug screening test given by a County appointed physician before the first day of employment. An offer of employment is contingent upon the results of the medical examination and drug screening test. Applicants for County employment may be subject to a post-offer criminal background check, depending on the nature and assignment of the position. When such check is conducted, an offer of employment is contingent upon the results of the criminal background check. Appointees must satisfactorily complete a probationary period before the appointment will be considered permanent.

piExternOpen.Job Description:
**Please note that, while the priority deadline for this position was 7/1/2026, we will continue to accept new applications in July and early August and encourage you to apply as soon as possible.**

### **Summary**
The Youth Law Center (YLC) is seeking applications from third-year law students, judicial clerks, and other recent law graduates who are interested in working on advocacy related to access to public benefits—including but not limited to Social Security Administration benefits, housing programs, nutrition supports, and foster care benefits—for systems-impacted transition-aged youth (TAY) in California. **Fellowship candidates will apply for fellowship funding **(applications are typically due in Fall 2026) offered by the Skadden Fellowship Foundation, Equal Justice Works Foundation, and law-school-specific or other sponsored fellowships. **Please note that YLC will not independently fund this fellowship**, but we will cover any difference between the external funding obtained and the position salary according to our internal salary scale.
Candidates for this role should be self-starters with an interest in system-impact projects, particularly in the area of increasing access to public benefits programs for youth and young adults impacted by the child welfare and juvenile justice systems, and in working directly with California legal aid attorneys supporting those young people at home in their communities. This will be a remote position, based in California, with some opportunities to collaborate in-person with other California-based attorneys.

### **Position Detail **
Transition-aged youth in the juvenile justice and child welfare systems need an ecosystem of support, services, and opportunities that will allow them to thrive in adulthood. Many youth are left to navigate adulthood on their own, deeply traumatized by their experiences before system involvement, separation from their families, and their experiences in systems. Lacking relationships, post-secondary educational opportunities, financial stability, and job training, many struggle to access basic needs—including food, housing, transportation, and child care—as they transition to adulthood. YLC’s advocacy to support healthy transitions to adulthood for transition-aged youth is guided by the lived experiences of youth who are rewriting what’s possible for the next generation.
This fellowship project will build on that work, and address the unique needs of transition-aged youth in California at this particular moment, when federal actions further threaten access to the supports that these youth and young adults need to thrive. The project will include collaboration with California’s legal services network as a critical strategy for success.
Our staff will work closely with the selected candidate to develop a strong fellowship proposal for public benefits advocacy for TAY that will integrate well with YLC’s mission and related areas of focus. Candidates should be located in California, or be willing to relocate to California, and have taken or plan to take the California bar exam.

### **About YLC’s Advocacy**
YLC is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit legal advocacy organization that works to protect children in the nation’s foster care and justice systems from abuse and neglect and to ensure that they receive the necessary support and services to become healthy and productive adults. Since 1978, our lawyers have worked across the United States to reduce the use of out-of-home care and incarceration; ensure safe, humane, and developmentally appropriate conditions in out-of-home placements; keep children out of adult jails; and secure equitable treatment for children in the child welfare and juvenile justice systems. Our efforts have focused on strengthening families, and we advocate for education, medical and mental health, legal support, and transition services needed to assure children’s success in care and in the community. We fight for increased accountability of the juvenile justice and child welfare systems, and champion professional and public education.

### **Skills & Experience**
Factors that will be utilized in evaluating candidates include:
- Demonstrated commitment to public interest law
- Knowledge of, experience with, or strong interest in child welfare and/or juvenile justice issues
- Excellent written and oral communication skills
- Strong analytic ability and legal research skills
- Ability both to work independently in a remote-work environment and work well with others
- Anticipated or current bar membership, with strong preference given to applicants who are or will be members of the California Bar
- Ability to travel

**People of color and individuals who have lived experience in the child welfare and/or juvenile justice system are strongly encouraged to apply.**

### **Employment & Benefit Details**
- **Employment Status: **Full-time, exempt; one-year or two-year position (depending upon the term of the awarded fellowship), with the potential to extend into a full-time staff position in related work at the conclusion of the fellowship.
- **Salary:** Fellows are placed on the same salary scale as our Staff Attorneys, with a possible range of **$76,000 to $85,000** for fellows, depending on years of prior post-J.D. experience. All YLC staff are paid using an equitable pay structure with planned annual increases.
- **Paid Time Off:** Unlimited paid vacation, 13 accrued sick days annually, and 11+ paid holidays; paid parental leave after one year of service.
- **Benefits:** Medical (HMO & PPO options), dental, vision, long-term disability, and life insurance; EAP; healthcare and dependent care FSA plans; pre-tax commuter benefits plan; 401k with up to 4% employer match; remote workstation equipment; and a remote work expense reimbursement. Health plan premiums are currently 100% employer-paid for staff and all enrolled family members.
- **Location:** This position will be based in California and will be fully remote, with opportunities for in-person work with YLC’s other California-based staff members as relevant and needed for the project.

### **To Apply**
Please submit an application via the application form on this BambooHR job page. When you apply, you will be required to provide all of the following documents:
1. Cover letter, explaining your interest in YLC, including why you are specifically interested in working on a project related to access to public benefits for systems-impacted transition-aged youth in California. This letter should also outline any related work or life experience that would make you an excellent candidate for this position.
2. Resume
3. Writing sample
4. List of at least three academic or professional references

Please submit all required documents in either Word (.docx) or PDF format at the time of application. Incomplete applications will not be considered for this position.
**Timeline: **Applications are accepted on a rolling basis until this posting is closed, but priority will be given to applications received by July 1st, 2026, as interviews will take place during the summer.
If you have questions about this position or the application process, feel free to contact us at **[careers@ylc.org](mailto:careers@ylc.org)**, but please do not email your application materials to this email address. Note that due to the volume of applications we receive, we may not be able to respond to every inquiry in detail. No phone calls about the position, please.

### **About the Youth Law Center**
YLC’s mission is to transform foster care and juvenile justice systems across the nation so every child and youth can thrive. Our goal is to ensure that, whenever a system must intervene in the life of a child, that child will receive the supports, services, and excellent parenting they need to become a flourishing adult. YLC’s specific, actionable, and sustainable advocacy strategies are shaped by the voices of youth and families most impacted by these systems and are informed by research in child development, psychology, behavioral economics, marketing and branding, and adult learning. The YLC team reflects the diverse backgrounds, experiences, and skills needed to make our creative approach to advocacy successful. Find out more about us at **[ylc.org](https://ylc.org/)** and **[qpi4kids.org](http://qpi4kids.org/)**.

### **San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance**
Pursuant to the **[San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance](https://www.sf.gov/information--fair-chance-ordinance)**, we will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records for employment.

### **Equal Opportunity Employer**
YLC values a diverse, inclusive workforce, and we provide equal employment opportunity for all applicants and employees. All qualified applicants for employment will be considered without regard to an individual’s actual or perceived race, color, sex, gender identity, gender expression, religion, age, body size, hair style, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, physical or mental disability, neurotypicality, medical condition, family care status, marital status, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local laws.

### **Diversity, Equity & Inclusion**
Read our full DEI statement **[here](https://www.ylc.org/about/diversity-equity-inclusion-statement/)**.
